newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hundreds stranded in HK by India air strike.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds stranded in HK by India air strike.

text.p: Airlines in Hong Kong packed of some 800 passengers to hotels after their flights were cancelled because of a nationwide strike by Indian air traffic controllers, an airport spokesman said on Saturday.

Up to 14 flights to or from India and the Middle East have been suspended since Friday afternoon due to the strike, but the spokesman said the 800 passengers affected on Friday had been taken care of.
"As for those who tried checking in yesterday, the airlines concerned had arranged accomodation for them, so no one was stuck at the airport," the spokesman said by telephone.

Three passenger flights and one cargo flight were either cancelled or delayed on Friday. One passenger flight was destined for Dubai, but had to be cancelled as it would pass through Indian airspace, the spokesman said.
He said Hong Kong air traffic controllers received notice of the strike from their Indian counterparts and were able to inform Saturday's passengers ahead of time.
"Our air traffic controllers received a message around 3 pm (0700 GMT) yesterday that Indian airports were on strike," he said.
"We were informed early, so the airlines informed passengers that they won't need to come to the airport today. Those affected today, they wouldn't have come," he said.
Ten flights were suspended on Saturday, five of which either originate or are destined for Dubai.
But the spokesman said he doubted if the airlines concerned would have found other routes to Dubai.
"It's not easy to find alternative routes, the Indian subcontinent stretches (far south) and it's very difficult to go all the way down and over," he said.
